To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and characterized cacaoidin, the first member of a new RiPP class, the lanthidins, and we have identified its biosynthetic gene locus, which is distinct from those of other known RiPPs.
we have identified and characterized a novel glycosylation RiPP, cacaoidin.
we have discovered a new lantibiotic with a unique structure that belongs to a new RiPP class and that is active against Clostridium spp., including C. difficile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of novel RiPPs, with their structural and biosynthetic analysis and with the discovery of new antibiotics.
the discovery and characterization of a new RiPP with an unprecedented structural motif and with the identification of a new RiP biosynthetic pathway.
the discovery of a new family of antimicrobial RiPPs, the lanthidins, with the identification of cacaoidin as their first representative.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cacaoidin represents the first example of the lanthidin family.
cacaoidin is the first representative of a new RiPP class.
the cacaoidin biosynthetic gene is a new RiPP pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new lantibiotic from a Streptmyces cacaoi isolate, and that we have identified the first member of a new lanthidins RiPP family.
cacaoidin, the first member of a new RiPP lanthidin family, is a potent lantibiotic that could be further exploited for the treatment of infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria.
the new RiPP family of lanthidins is introduced, the biosynthetic pathway is proposed and a new lantibiotic is described.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the discovery and characterization of novel RiPPs is a continuous process and that the identification of a novel RiPP family is possible.
a new family of RiPPs, named lanthidins, is emerging, and it is characterized by a new type of thioether cross-link.

the discovery of a novel family of RiPPs with an unusual structure, and the identification of the gene cluster encoding the biosynthetic machinery, opens new perspectives in the field of natural product research.
